idea: A linear equation simplifies to ax+b=cx+d. It has no solution when the x-coefficients match but the constants don't (a=c, b=d), and infinitely many when both match. Expand and collect before comparing.
trap: Setting the constants equal when the question asks for no solution, or comparing coefficients before distributing.
desmos: Graphing both sides shows parallel lines (no solution) or one line (infinitely many), but only after you know the constant. With an unknown constant, compare coefficients by hand.

items.stem: In the equation 3(x−8)−1=kx−12, k is a constant. For what value of k does the equation have no solution?
items.explain: Expand the left side: 3x−25. No solution means the x-terms match and the constants differ. So k=3; the constants −25 and −12 are different, so the equation has no solution.

items.stem: In the equation 5(6x+4)=ax+b, a and b are constants. If the equation has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of a+b?

items.stem: In the equation 2x+1​+5x−6​=kx​, k is a constant. For what value of k does the equation have no solution?
items.explain: Combine the left side: the x-coefficient is 21​+51​=107​ and the constant is 21​−56​=−107​. The right side has x-coefficient k1​ and constant 0. No solution needs equal x-coefficients and unequal constants: k1​=107​, so k=710​.
